drugs.indication: Analgesia (background / breakthrough pain) — Prolonged Casualty Care
drugs.rate: slow IV/IO push; repeat q10-30 min PRN (titrate to PAIN RELIEF)
drugs.notes: CPG-61: Ketamine push (for pain) 20 mg (0.1-0.2 mg/kg) IV/IO q10-30 min PRN; if no IV/IO, quadruple to 80 mg IM (0.4-0.8 mg/kg). ENDPOINT = PAIN RELIEF; NYSTAGMUS = SEDATION (overshoot), NOT analgesia. START LOW, GO SLOW. Rapid push >1 mg/kg -> respiratory depression. >1.5 mg/kg adds no extra effect. 0.3-0.8 mg/kg = highest adverse/emergence reactions. Meds table: pain 20 mg IV / range 0.1-0.2 mg/kg IV / sedation 1 mg/kg IV.
drugs.source_citation: JTS CPG 61 footnote 1 (Ketamine push for pain 20 mg / 0.1-0.2 mg/kg IV/IO q10-30 min; IM 80 mg / 0.4-0.8 mg/kg) + Meds table row (Ketamine 20 mg IV / 0.1-0.2 mg/kg IV / 1 mg/kg IV sedation)

drugs.indication: Sedation — loading dose before continuous infusion
drugs.rate: slow IV/IO push over 60 seconds; start the continuous drip ~10-15 min later
drugs.notes: Endpoint of effect: nystagmus. Rapid push >1 mg/kg -> respiratory depression. Loading dose always precedes the drip.
drugs.source_version: JTS CPG ID 61 (11 May 2017); transcribed via UA translation — confirm vs EN original
drugs.source_citation: PCC Analgesia & Sedation — footnote 3 + Appendix B (loading 1 mg/kg IV/IO over 60 s)

drugs.indication: Continuous sedation — IV/IO drip (Prolonged Casualty Care)
drugs.rate: continuous infusion after the 1 mg/kg loading; titrate by 0.25 mg/kg/h (one table row); drum-drip start rate ml/h = patient weight(kg) / 2

infusion.concentration: 3 mg/ml (750 mg = 1.5 amp of 500 mg/5 ml, in 250 ml NS)

drugs.notes: Appendix B numeric drip tables (mg/kg/h, mcg/kg/min, ml/hr for 40/60/80/100 kg; drops/min for 15 and 10 gtt/ml sets) NOT transcribed numerically yet — transcribe + verify from source (TODO). Drum-drip regulator inaccurate <10 ml/h -> use drop-count method. This guide frames the infusion as SEDATION; a low-dose analgesia-only ketamine drip is not specified here. Endpoint: nystagmus. Rapid >1 mg/kg -> respiratory depression; >1.5 mg/kg no added effect. NOTE: this is the SEDATION drip (3 mg/ml); see pcc_ketamine_analgesia_infusion for the analgesia drip (1 mg/ml).
drugs.source_version: JTS CPG ID 61 (11 May 2017); transcribed via UA translation — confirm vs EN original
drugs.source_citation: PCC Analgesia & Sedation — Appendix B (mix 750 mg / 250 ml NS = 3 mg/ml; 1 mg/kg/h non-intubated, 1-2 mg/kg/h intubated) + Appendix D

drugs.indication: Continuous ANALGESIA — IV/IO drip (Prolonged Casualty Care)
drugs.dose_per_kg: drip 0.1-0.2 mg/kg/h (after a 0.2-0.3 mg/kg priming bolus)
drugs.rate: PRIMING BOLUS first (analgesia must be established before the drip): 0.2-0.3 mg/kg (guideline 20-30 mg fixed; Owner uses 0.2 mg/kg then assesses effect). THEN hang the continuous drip at 0.1-0.2 mg/kg/h; titrate to pain relief.

infusion.concentration: 1 mg/ml — STANDARD (1 ml = 1 mg). Prep: 100 mg (2 ml of 50 mg/ml ketamine) in 100 ml NS.

drugs.notes: ANALGESIA drip. Dose range 0.1-0.2 mg/kg from CPG-61 Appendix C; the Owner runs it as a continuous 1 mg/ml infusion at 0.1-0.2 mg/kg/h after a 0.2-0.3 mg/kg priming bolus. Distinct from the CPG-61 Appendix B ketamine SEDATION drip (3 mg/ml, 1 mg/kg/h). Endpoint = pain relief; NYSTAGMUS = sedation overshoot, avoid. Run-time example: 100 mg/100 ml, 5 gtt/min on 20 gtt/ml = 15 ml/h -> ~6.6 h.
drugs.source_citation: JTS CPG-61, Appendix C (Common IV Meds Cheat Sheet): Ketamine analgesia pain dose range 0.1-0.2 mg/kg IV (moderate pain 20 mg IV; sedation 1 mg/kg IV); START LOW, GO SLOW. Owner drip prep: 100 mg in 100 ml NS (1 mg/ml), priming 0.2-0.3 mg/kg then continuous 0.1-0.2 mg/kg/h.

drugs.drug: Burn resuscitation fluid — Lactated Ringer's (preferred); normal saline 0.9% if LR unavailable
drugs.indication: Burn shock fluid resuscitation — Prolonged Casualty Care (>20% TBSA)
drugs.route: IV/IO infusion (NG or rectal electrolyte solution as alternatives)
drugs.fixed_dose: initial rate by Rule of Ten: %TBSA x 10 ml/h (+100 ml/h per 10 kg over 80 kg)
drugs.rate: start fluids during primary assessment (initial ~500 ml/h); then Rule of Ten rate; TITRATE to urine output 30-50 ml/h in adults (peds 0.5-1 ml/kg/h) by adjusting +/-25% every 1-2 h; do NOT 'catch up' volume if delayed

infusion.diluent: BEST: isotonic crystalloid — Lactated Ringer's (preferred) or Plasmalyte. IF UNAVAILABLE: normal saline 0.9% is acceptable. (TCCC 2026 §15.e: LR, NS, or Hextend; Hextend max 1000 ml then LR/NS.)
infusion.diluent_volume_ml: per resuscitation need (24 h planning volume via Parkland)
infusion.target_rate: %TBSA x 10 ml/h (+100/10kg over 80 kg); titrate to urine 30-50 ml/h

drugs.notes: Parkland (4 ml x kg x %TBSA) is for 24-h PLANNING only; hourly resuscitation starts with the Rule of Ten. TCCC permissive/hypotensive resuscitation does NOT apply to burns unless major hemorrhage. Concordant with TCCC 2026 Rule of Ten (formula burn_rule_of_ten). If urine cannot be measured: keep HR<140, palpable peripheral pulse, good capillary refill, normal mental status. FLUID CHOICE (Owner direction 2026-07-13): best = Lactated Ringer's (or Plasmalyte); if LR is not available, normal saline 0.9% is acceptable (PCC burns 'Best: isotonic crystalloids (LR, Plasmalyte)' + TCCC 2026 §15.e lists LR, NS, or Hextend).
drugs.source_version: JTS burn PFC CPG (UA translation, tccc.org.ua), 2026-07-13 — confirm ID/version
drugs.source_citation: JTS Burn PFC CPG (UA) — Fluid Resuscitation section + Appendix D (Rule of Ten; LR/Plasmalyte; urine 30-50 ml/h; adjust +/-25%); fluid choice: PCC burns 'Найкраще: ізотонічні кристалоїди (Рінгер Лактат, Плазмаліт)' + TCCC 2026 §15.e (LR, NS, or Hextend)

drugs.indication: Priming analgesia bolus before the analgesia drip
drugs.rate: slow IV/IO push BEFORE hanging the drip; Owner uses 0.2 mg/kg then assesses effect (guideline analgesia range 0.1-0.2 mg/kg)
drugs.notes: Priming ('working') analgesic dose before the 1 mg/ml drip. Endpoint: pain relief; NYSTAGMUS = sedation overshoot, avoid.
drugs.source_version: JTS CPG ID 61 (11 May 2017); Owner priming practice — confirm
drugs.source_citation: Owner priming practice before the analgesia drip (0.2-0.3 mg/kg); CPG-61 ketamine analgesia push range 0.1-0.2 mg/kg

formulas.name: Gravity IV drip rate
formulas.applicability: Gravity infusion set. drop_factor in {10,15,20,60,custom} gtt/ml. Output rounded to whole drops.
formulas.notes: Deterministic arithmetic identity, not a clinical recommendation; exempt from Owner clinical verification but shown with source tag. Example: 500 ml / 240 min * 20 = 41.67 -> 42 gtt/min.
formulas.source_citation: Standard drip-rate identity (volume/time x drop factor)

formulas.name: Burn initial fluid rate — USAISR Rule of Ten (TCCC)
formulas.expression: initial_rate_ml_per_hr = TBSA_percent * 10 ; if weight_kg > 80 then add 100 ml/hr for each full 10 kg above 80
formulas.applicability: Adults 40-80 kg base; TBSA > 20%. Initiate as soon as IV/IO access established. If hemorrhagic shock also present, shock resuscitation takes precedence. Consider oral fluids for burns up to 30% TBSA if conscious.
formulas.notes: Resuscitation fluid: Lactated Ringer's, normal saline, or Hextend (Hextend max 1000 ml, then LR/NS). Estimate TBSA to nearest 10% by Rule of Nines.
formulas.source_citation: TFC §15 Burns, e Fluid resuscitation (USAISR Rule of Ten): %TBSA x 10 ml/hr for 40-80 kg; +100 ml/hr per 10 kg above 80 kg

formulas.name: Weight-based infusion -> ml/h and drops per minute
formulas.expression: ml_per_h = dose_mg_per_kg_per_h * weight_kg / concentration_mg_per_ml ; gtt_per_min = round(ml_per_h * drop_factor / 60)
formulas.applicability: Continuous weight-based IV infusion on a gravity set. drop_factor in {10,15,20,60} gtt/ml. Concentration + dose rate come from a VERIFIED drug record; this formula only does arithmetic.
formulas.notes: Validated vs JTS CPG-61 Appendix B (3 mg/ml sedation ml/h for 40/60/80/100 kg match exactly). Example: 0.2 mg/kg/h, 80 kg, 1 mg/ml, 20 gtt/ml -> ml/h 16, gtt/min 5.
formulas.source_citation: Deterministic infusion arithmetic; cross-checked vs JTS CPG-61 Appendix B
